title: Uncertainty intervals
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of uncertainty intervals
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up

prerequisite.prompt: Recall Sampling variability. Explain why a recorded result needs its input conditions and evidence source before it can support a claim.
prerequisite.answer: A result depends on the inputs, procedure and conditions that produced it. Preserve data roles and distinguish observed outcomes from predictions or unmeasured conditions. If the prior concept cannot be explained, use a short retrieval activity before this chapter.

vocabulary: The model-based variation of an estimate
An interval procedure with declared repeated-sampling coverage
A supplied population standard deviation assumption

blocks.text: An uncertainty interval needs a sampling model and assumptions. A confidence level refers to the repeated-sampling method, not a probability attached to a fixed unknown parameter after observing data.

Begin by writing the question the procedure is intended to answer. Identify the information already supplied, the information it will produce and the information still missing. These are constructed classroom examples; they do not require live accounts, private records or an external service. Do not treat a plausible explanation as a measured outcome.

For this constructed exercise assume independent normal measurements with known population standard deviation2. A95% mean interval uses supplied normal critical value1.96:mean plus/minus1.96*sigma/sqrt(n). Unknown sigma requires a different justified method.

If a required input is absent or violates the stated contract, record that condition explicitly instead of quietly replacing it with a convenient value.

Compare the intermediate evidence with the final statement. Explain why each number or decision follows from the stated inputs. The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

Optional local lab: predict the printed result before running this standalone Python 3 example. Change one relevant boundary input, record the outcome and state the contract or statistical assumptions. The program uses fictional values and the Python standard library; it performs no external operations.

lesson.title: Check the boundary and the interpretation

blocks.text: A narrow interval can be precisely biased; sampling independence and representativeness must be justified.

A useful check asks what would make the reasoning fail. Distinguish a failure to execute the declared procedure from a weakness in the procedure itself. The first may require a correction; the second requires an explicitly revised method and new evidence. Preserve unsuccessful cases so an improved result cannot hide the original problem.

blocks.label: Guided: restate the worked result, then name the assumption or limitation that prevents a broader conclusion.

lesson.title: Apply the idea and plan the next check

blocks.text: Complete the supported workbook tasks before attempting W4 independently. Record any hints or help used. After feedback, use the teacher's fresh retry rather than copying the earlier answer. For a project, select a relevant new case, predict the outcome from the declared rule and preserve the result alongside any revision.

blocks.label: Exit: propose one revealing change to the worked scenario. State the expected outcome and the evidence that would make you revise your explanation.

workbook.prompt: Explain the weekly mechanism in your own words. Use the worked scenario to name its input, decision rule and output.

workbook.prompt: Observed mean10, n16, sigma2. Compute standard error, margin and interval. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.

workbook.title: Audit the limit
workbook.prompt: A report omits this qualification: A narrow interval can be precisely biased; sampling independence and representativeness must be justified. Explain how omitting it could change a reader's interpretation, and write an accurate replacement.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: A narrow interval can be precisely biased; sampling independence and representativeness must be justified. State the observed result separately from the unverified or out-of-scope claim; preserve the original evidence rather than inventing a missing fact.

workbook.title: Apply a new case independently
workbook.prompt: Mean20, n25, known sigma5 and critical1.96. Compute interval and name one assumption.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: SE1, margin1.96, interval[18.04, 21.96]. Require independent normal sampling and known sigma; bias is not repaired by the interval.

workbook.title: Design a revealing follow-up
workbook.prompt: For the worked scenario, propose one additional case that could reveal a failure, describe its expected outcome before running it, and explain what would need to remain fixed for a fair comparison. Do not reuse W4 as a new final test after receiving feedback.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Accept a concrete variant of the worked input or a missing/conflicting/boundary condition, with an expectation derived from the declared procedure. Require preserved settings, original outputs and data roles. A narrow interval can be precisely biased; sampling independence and representativeness must be justified. The new case should test this particular mechanism rather than merely restate the original result.

teacher.background: Two 45-minute sessions. An uncertainty interval needs a sampling model and assumptions. A confidence level refers to the repeated-sampling method, not a probability attached to a fixed unknown parameter after observing data. Use the supplied constructed scenarios to make the mechanism inspectable. Collect W4 before sharing solutions. Students should name intermediate evidence and limitations; classroom pacing and learning effectiveness remain unvalidated.
materials: Lesson and workbook; paper and pencil
Calculator and optional local Python 3 for arithmetic; no live API or private data
Prepare the fresh retry separately and withhold its solution until after collection
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite; identify the input, procedure and evidence source.
Explain section 1 and vocabulary. Complete W1 with a mechanism-based explanation.
Trace the declared procedure and worked case. Complete W2, recording intermediate steps.
Discuss the diagram with the worked input; use W3 to distinguish measured claims and limitations.
Retrieve the worked reasoning and collect the guided response before discussing it.
Compare a proposed boundary variant with the original case; identify what remains fixed.
Collect W4 independently. Require the procedure trace and the bounded conclusion.
Use W5 and exit responses for feedback. Administer the fresh retry after feedback and preserve both attempts.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: SE=2/4=.5; margin=.98; interval[9.02, 10.98]. Under assumptions, the method covers the fixed population mean in95% of repeated samples. Qualification: A narrow interval can be precisely biased; sampling independence and representativeness must be justified. Exit: accept a concrete variation with its predicted outcome and a stated condition that would challenge the mechanism; reject a claim resting on unmeasured evidence.
misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A narrow interval can be precisely biased; sampling independence and representativeness must be justified.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
teacher.assessment: W4: SE1, margin1.96, interval[18.04, 21.96]. Require independent normal sampling and known sigma; bias is not repaired by the interval. Require intermediate reasoning and the stated scope. Fresh retry: Mean8, n16, known sigma4. Expected reasoning: SE1, margin1.96, interval[6.04, 9.96] under the same assumptions. If students need support, record it and reassess with another new case rather than awarding independence to a copied answer.
teacher.support: Provide an input/procedure/result/limit frame and a calculator when needed. Ask students to identify the first step before completing the whole trace. Extension: compare two concrete variants of this mechanism while holding unrelated conditions fixed; report both successful and unsuccessful outcomes.
teacher.next: Next connection: Effect size and practical importance. Preserve the current case record and retrieve its evidence boundary before moving on.
